title: Minimoog: Emerson's Fat Bass

phrase.transcribed_with: transcribe_mono.py <clip> <begin> <end> 17 55 110 16 80 (the 32' oscillator is tracked; the key is two octaves above it; every note comes out struck)

reference: A real Minimoog Model D set to this chart and played by SynthMania ("Minimoog Sound Charts by Tom Rhea", YouTube, copyrighted: kept in the audition folder for this comparison only). Two stretches of the riff, thirty notes; the stretch between them is left out because the player bends notes with the pitch wheel there. My rebuild plays the same notes, transcribed from the recording, every one struck anew as in the recording.
source: Tom Rhea's Sound Charts for the Minimoog (Moog Music, 1974), page 15: oscillators, levels and switches as charted; the cutoff from the dial by the service manual's calibration. The filter's contour amount, emphasis, the contours' times and sustain are fitted to the recording. The chart's slight shaking of the filter by oscillator 3 is not in it.

reference: A real Minimoog Model D set to this chart and played by SynthMania ("Minimoog Sound Charts by Tom Rhea", YouTube, copyrighted: kept in the audition folder for this comparison only). My rebuild plays the same notes, transcribed from the recording. That instrument is 30 cents sharp; the rebuild is tuned to it for this clip.
source: Tom Rhea's Sound Charts for the Minimoog (Moog Music, 1974), page 15: ranges, levels and switches as charted. Fitted to the recording: the pulse width (that instrument's square wave is nearer a third than a half), cutoff, emphasis, the contour's reach and time. No glide, though the chart has it on: the recording's notes change at once.

title: Prophet-5: Sync II
reference: A real Prophet-5 Rev 3 playing factory program 32, recorded by SynthMania (copyrighted: kept in the audition folder for this comparison only). Four single notes cut out of the demonstration, three low and one high (the player bends most of the high ones with the pitch wheel, so they cannot be compared); my rebuild plays the same notes for the same lengths, each at the pitch the recording has it (that instrument is a fifth of a semitone sharp, and further off in its top octaves).
source: Sequential's own factory data for program 3-2 (the 2020 Prophet-5's factory bank, which holds the original forty programs, and the 1978 patch sheet), with the service manual's calibration: oscillators, pulse width, Poly-Mod depth, envelope shape. The filter envelope's reach, the cutoff and the decay time are fitted to the recording.

title: Prophet-5: Brass
reference: A real Prophet-5 Rev 3 playing factory program 11, recorded by SynthMania (copyrighted: kept in the audition folder for this comparison only). Five chords cut out of the demonstration, each from its start to just before the player brings in the wheel's vibrato: A minor seventh, F, G, C, E minor. My rebuild plays the same chords and is cut at the same moments.
source: Sequential's own factory data for program 1-1 with the service manual's calibration: oscillator, the filter's reach, the envelopes' shapes. The cutoff, the envelopes' times and their sustain levels are fitted to those five chords.

title: Contact opening: the first synth
reference: The Sherbs, "We Ride Tonight" (1981), the record Daft Punk sampled for "Contact": its first synth, playing alone (copyrighted: kept in the audition folder for this comparison only). My rebuild plays the chords as I could read them from the recording; a few inner notes may be wrong. The record runs 15 cents sharp; the rebuild is tuned to it for this clip.
source: No published settings: nobody has said which instrument this is. Built from what the recording shows (two sawtooth oscillators a note, 17 cents apart; one steep low-pass that opens at each note and closes over seconds), then fitted to it.
